MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.claim: The greatest losers in deeds are the Christian monks living in cells.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.claim: Hell is prepared for unbelievers; the next question introduces the people who lose most through their deeds.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the people's effort goes astray, though they think they are doing well; Yaḥyā identifies them as the People of the Book.

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.claim: أعمالا is a specification after الأخسرين, clarifying the type of loss.

NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.speaker: حمزة
NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.claim: The author judges Hamza’s reading more correct, following Sibawayh’s concern about assimilating lām into nūn, although that assimilation is possible at a distance because the articulation points are close.

NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.claim: ‘The greatest losers in deeds’ uses an accusative of specification.

SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.claim: People ruin their good works by reproaching recipients and demanding thanks, and ruin worship by performing it for show and reputation.

THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.claim: He identifies the greatest losers as monks and priests who confined themselves in cloisters.

THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عباس
THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.claim: They identify them as Jews and Christians, comparing the claim with the description of weary workers entering a blazing fire.

THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa about the greatest losers, he answers that they are the people of Harura, the Kharijites.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.claim: The worst in deeds are priests and monks.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.claim: They are Jews and Christians among the People of the Book.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.claim: Another report identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies them as followers of religious whims.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.claim: Another interpretation is people who do good deeds and boast of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.claim: Possible referents are hypocrites whose deeds contradict belief, or people who seek this world and abandon the next.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.claim: A further possible referent is those who seek this world and abandon the next.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.claim: The question asks about people whose deeds make them the greatest losers among creation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as disbelieving People of the Book.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies them as Jews and Christians.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.claim: One report from Ali identifies them as monks living in cells.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.claim: Another report from Ali identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.claim: God asks whether people should be told of those whose deeds are most disastrously lost.

JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.claim: The passage affirms Gog and Magog and the trumpet blast as signs of the Hour.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.claim: Those who assume worship of others benefits them are the greatest losers: they exhaust themselves in deeds they think right, then end in the Fire.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.speaker: علي
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.claim: A report says the verse about the greatest losers was revealed concerning monks and priests who confined themselves in monasteries.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص، ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.claim: Another report identifies the greatest losers as Jews and Christians.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.claim: Abu Ali reports that it was revealed concerning the people of Haruraʾ.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.claim: Al-Asamm strongly rejects the Haruriyya report because the verse calls them unbelievers in God's signs while they are Muslims.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.claim: If the report from Ali is authentic, it must be accepted; kufr here can mean rejecting some of God's signs, as rebels do.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.claim: The greatest losers exhaust themselves in work expecting reward but end in ruin, like a merchant who buys expecting profit and loses.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.claim: They identify the losers as Jews and Christians.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as monks who confined themselves to monasteries.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.claim: He identifies them as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.claim: The question about the greatest losers is a taunting rebuke addressed to the disbelievers.

TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.claim: The greatest losers in works are disbelieving Jews and Christians whose efforts in worldly life came to nothing while they thought their actions were virtuous acts of obedience and worship.

TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.speaker: العياشي
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the greatest losers: Ali identified scriptural communities who disbelieved and innovated, adding that the Khawarij were not far from them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.speaker: علي والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the worst losers as Christian priests and monks.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.claim: Another view identifies them as Jews and Christians.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.claim: أعمالا is an accusative specification: الأخسرين alone leaves unclear what was lost, so أعمالا names the kind of loss.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.speaker: سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.claim: In a Bukhari report, Saʿd says the worst losers are Jews and Christians, not the Khawarij: Jews denied Muhammad, and Christians denied Paradise’s food and drink; he called the Khawarij covenant-breakers and wicked.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.claim: The question rebukes disbelievers who worship other than God: their efforts and hopes fail, making them the greatest losers in deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.claim: Ali identifies the worst losers as the Khawarij of Harura; on another occasion he names the monks in their cells, and tells Ibn al-Kawwa that he and his companions are meant.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya says these identifications are weakened by the following description of people who disbelieved God’s signs and meeting Him; that fits Meccan idolaters, though Ali and Saʿd named groups that share aspects of the warning.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.claim: The verses show that people may work while imagining their deeds good even though their effort is nullified; the cause is corrupt belief or ostentation, and here specifically disbelief.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.claim: The accusative aʿmālan is a specification; it is plural because it modifies active agents or because their deeds are diverse.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.claim: A plural tamyīz is used where singular would be expected to express the many kinds of desires; the referents are the People of the Book or monks.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.claim: Ali identifies the greatest losers as monks, by analogy with the “toiling, weary” phrase.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.speaker: مجاهد، author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.claim: Mujahid says the People of the Book; other views say the Sabians or, in Ali's answer to Ibn al-Kawwa, the Harurites. The author treats these as examples, not an exhaustive definition: the label covers those outside Islam, show-offs, and heretics whose innovations lead to unbelief.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.claim: Alladhīna may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted “they are,” or accusative for censure; the next clause can then be its description or apposition.

SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.claim: أعمالا is a specification of الأخسرين and is plural because the kinds of deeds differ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.claim: Asked whether the greatest losers are the Haruriyya, Sa'd answers that they are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied food and drink in Paradise; the Haruriyya break God's covenant after pledging it, and Sa'd called them profligates. Bukhari transmits this.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.claim: Ali, al-Dahhak, and others identify the greatest losers as the Haruriyya.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.claim: The verse broadly includes the Haruriyya alongside Jews, Christians, and others; it is not exclusive to any group, since it is Meccan, before the relevant Jewish-Christian address and before the Khawarij existed. It covers anyone who follows an unapproved way while thinking the work is accepted, as echoed in 88:2–4, 25:23, and 24:39.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.claim: The greatest losers are those whose efforts were invalid under a lawful, pleasing religious way, yet who believe they are doing well and that their deeds are accepted and loved.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to warn those heedless of remembrance, whose eyes and ears fail to take in the warning, about the greatest losers.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.claim: Their deeds vary: some worship angels, stars, prophets, or idols, while others commit different forms of unbelief.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits from Saʿd that the greatest losers are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied Paradise has food or drink.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.claim: The author adds that both groups deny bodily resurrection and restrict the afterlife to a spiritual one.

DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.claim: Sa'd rejects identifying the greatest losers as the Kharijites and instead names Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, Christians denied food and drink in Paradise, while Kharijites break God's covenant and were called transgressors.

DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.claim: In another report Sa'd names monastic ascetics and the Kharijites as people who strayed, whereupon God caused their hearts to stray.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.claim: Ali identifies the greatest losers as monks who confined themselves to pillars.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked, Ali identified the greatest losers as Quraysh's transgressors.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.claim: Ali also thought the Kharijites were included among those described as the greatest losers.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.claim: Ka'b says the Quran appears as a beautiful, fragrant companion to the person who acted by it, soothes his terror, and identifies itself as his good deeds.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.claim: The Quran asks God to intercede for its companion, reminding Him that it occupied his days with thirst and nights with wakefulness; he is then crowned and robed in honor.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.claim: The Prophet, together with the believers who follow him, is commanded to tell the unbelievers about the greatest losers in deeds.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.claim: أخسرين أعمالا is an accusative of specification; its plural signals varied kinds of deeds and means the greatest loss among creatures.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad reads this as unbelievers whose deeds were good in themselves, such as charity and freeing slaves, and who proudly expected reward from them.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.claim: The question addresses unbelievers; if read as seeking their leave to announce the news, it is deeply sarcastic.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.claim: The plural “we” either immediately identifies the speaker or signals that believers already know this news as well.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.claim: أعمالا is an accusative specification; it is plural because it means “workers,” whereas a source noun used as specification can remain singular.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.claim: An alternative says أعمالا is a rare plural of عامل; some grammarians deny such plurals outside a few established words.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.claim: Another proposal treats أعمالا as plural of عمل, meaning people possessed of deeds; the author finds this strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.claim: The passage contrasts unbelievers’ intrinsically good acts, which they admire and expect reward for, with their intrinsically bad acts that they mistakenly deem good.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.claim: The passage answers those who worship useless idols as patrons and seek their favor, making their work and effort futile; the key rebuke is that they think they do well.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.claim: Beginning with the command say signals an important utterance deserving attentive listening.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.claim: The question whether to inform them is an offer used ironically: the speaker will inform them regardless of their assent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, building curiosity before revealing that the losers are the listeners themselves.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.claim: The polytheists are addressed to rebuke them and alert them to the failure of their efforts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.claim: The plural nūn in nunabbiʾukum may be God’s majestic plural, with narrative shift from expected he informs you.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.claim: Alternatively, the plural nūn may refer to the Messenger together with God, or to the Messenger and Muslims.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.claim: These six verses draw a conclusion from the sūrah’s account of worldly seduction, reliance on protectors besides God, spiritual blindness, and bad outcomes, and prepare for the closing declaration at 18:110.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.claim: The indirect address in “shall We inform you” targets polytheists, made explicit by the later description of those who disbelieved in God’s signs and meeting Him; the plural “deeds” stresses their varied losses.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.claim: People direct their efforts toward their aims: seeking God’s pleasure and the afterlife leads to one kind of work, while pursuit of worldly gain leads to another.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.claim: Polytheists think their idols bring them nearer to God and that shirk is obedience, but God gives their deeds no value in this life or the next.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.claim: Those who commit the evils described in these verses will be punished in Hell.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.claim: In Arabic, akhsar means greater loss than khasir, so the comparative form marks a more severe degree of loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.claim: The people described in Hud block both themselves and others from God's path, unlike those in Nahl who block only themselves; they are therefore more grievously lost.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.claim: Grammarians explain la jarama as an oath, or as meaning truly/rightfully; each reading gives emphasis.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.claim: Hud adds several charges beyond Naml, including blocking God's path and lying against God, so it emphatically calls its offenders the worst losers; Naml lacks that added emphasis.

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.claim: The greatest losers are those who disbelieve in God’s signs and meeting Him, because their worldly efforts are futile.
